assessments.zone: Rural Mutshatsha territory west of Kolwezi (Mutshatsha health zone: Mutshatsha town 'Quartier Commercial', Kayembe, Tshinaweji, Lufupa, Kaleji, Tambo, Kazovu, Mafunga, Mulomba/Disombo)
assessments.evidence: Sparsely populated rural territory along the Benguela railway with no reported armed-group activity; the territorial administration and PNC posts in Mutshatsha centre and larger villages are the state presence, with customary chiefs handling day-to-day disputes in remote villages. No sources could be retrieved in this run.

assessments.zone: Peri-urban and mining-belt villages around Kolwezi (Lualaba, Kanzenze, Dilala, Vangu health zones: Kitumayini, Tshikala/Lualaba Gare, Kawama, Mutanda, Kisanfu, Kamoa, Musokantanda, Mushima, etc.)
assessments.evidence: Mining towns and villages along the Kolwezi-Likasi road and around the Kamoa-Kakula, Mutanda, Kisanfu and Kamoto concessions, policed by the PNC/mines police with company security and occasional FARDC deployments at mine sites. No reported armed-group presence; Bakata Katanga activity is reported far to the east/north-east (s1).

assessments.zone: Kolwezi city (Manika and Dilala communes; all health-area neighbourhoods incl. Kasulo, Musompo, Mutoshi, Camp Massard) and the Kanzenze/Dilala urban extension (Luilu, Noa, Tshala, Tshamundenda, Inga, UCK, Kabila)
assessments.evidence: Provincial capital with full state administration; the PNC (including the mines and hydrocarbons police) runs commissariats, arrests and order, while FARDC and Republican Guard units are garrisoned in the city and deployed around industrial concessions. Crime and clashes between artisanal miners and security forces do not amount to territorial control by any non-state group. No specific 2025-2026 sources could be retrieved in this run.

units.CD7202-mutshatsha: This unit covers Kolwezi, capital of Lualaba province and the heart of the DRC copper/cobalt belt, its Dilala/Kanzenze urban extensions and surrounding mining villages, plus rural Mutshatsha territory to the west. No armed group is known to hold territory here: the state controls the whole unit, with the PNC (including the mines police) keeping order in Kolwezi's neighbourhoods, mining towns and villages, and FARDC and Republican Guard elements deployed in the city and around major industrial mining concessions. Insecurity is criminal and mining-related (clashes between artisanal miners and police/security over concessions, banditry, illegal mining sites such as Kasulo), not territorial. Bakata Katanga militia activity in 2024-2026 was reported in northern Haut-Katanga/Haut-Lomami (Mitwaba, Pweto, Bukama, Malemba-Nkulu), not in Lualaba's mining belt. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the egress proxy), so the assessment rests on default state presence and background knowledge.
